subject: System Design
title: How CDNs Cache Content
description: A short lesson to help you apply How CDNs Cache Content.

hook.text: A user in Mumbai requests an image hosted in Virginia. The CDN serves a cached copy from a server in Mumbai.

buildup.text: CDNs store copies of content on edge servers at hundreds of locations worldwide, called PoPs.

discovery.text: On a cache hit, the edge server responds directly. On a miss, it fetches from the origin and caches the result.

twist.text: Cache invalidation is the hardest part. Stale content can be served for hours if TTLs are misconfigured.

climax.text: CDNs turn a global latency problem into a local one by placing content near every user.

punchline.text: CDNs cache content at the edge, close to every user.

quiz.question: What happens on a CDN cache miss?
options: The edge fetches from the origin server and caches the result
The user is redirected to the origin
